newsitem.title: JAPAN: Changes shrinking Japan c/a surplus continuing - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Changes shrinking Japan c/a surplus continuing - MOF.

text.p: Structural changes which have caused a decline in Japan's current account surplus will continue, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday.
Mitsuzuka said structural changes -- such as the shifting of production offshore by Japanese manufacturers -- had worked to reduce the surplus by increasing imports.
"Structural changes which have caused the surplus to shrink will continue and must continue," he said in a speech to journalists and business executives.
He added that in 1996, Japan's current account surplus fell to 1.4 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), less than half of the level three years ago.
